clue.text: Quickly concentrated, as bimbo might appear?

definitions.meaning: arriving rapidly and in great numbers, as blows or questions can come
a stereotyped bimbo is thought stupid (thick) and promiscuous (fast)

explanation.surface: A quick description of how a dim, flighty woman might come across.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the phrase into its two words: THICK in the sense of stupid and FAST in the old sense of loose in morals.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes things coming rapidly and densely, like questions at a press conference.

clue.text: Criminals getting this first offender put inside

indicators.note: put inside says one piece is placed within another, here the offender within this

parts.note: Eve was the first sinner, eating the forbidden fruit in Genesis

explanation.surface: Lawbreakers get this first-time culprit jailed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put inside' suggests sending someone to jail, but here it is the container signal; Eve counts as the first offender because she ate the forbidden fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Thieves are people who steal, a common kind of lawbreaker.

clue.text: Read up half of Asimov's account, seeing his name

indicators.note: in a down clue, reading up means taking the letters from bottom to top, backwards
half of points to the first half of the following word's letters

explanation.surface: Someone reads half of an Asimov story and spots the author's name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' takes ASI from Asimov, and 'Read up' turns it to ISA.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac was the first name of the science-fiction writer Asimov.

clue.text: Teases wool, perhaps — it's very simple

parts.note: to kid is to tease
stuff is a woollen fabric, so wool is an example of it

explanation.surface: Someone combs wool and finds the job easy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Teases wool' suggests carding fibres, but stuff is an old word for woven woollen cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Something childishly easy is described with this phrase, as fit for youngsters.

clue.text: Are characters leaving submarine looking up for cloud?

indicators.note: in a down clue, looking up means the remaining letters read from bottom to top
leaving says some letters go away from the word that follows

parts.note: the characters of are are its letters A, R and E

explanation.surface: Someone in a submarine looks up to ask whether that is a cloud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes A, R and E out of SUBMARINE to leave SUBMIN, which 'looking up' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: A nimbus is a dark rain cloud, the root of cumulonimbus.

clue.text: Autumn feathers don't work efficiently

parts.note: fall is the American word for autumn
down is soft fine feathers

explanation.surface: Autumn plumage is described as ineffective.
explanation.definitionFit: Plans or arguments that fail at some point are said to collapse in this way.

clue.text: Eliminating recurrences, oversee repaired sort of mechanism

indicators.note: something repaired has been put back together, so the letters are reassembled
recurrences are letters that come back again, so the repeated ones are removed

explanation.surface: To stop things happening again, someone oversees the fixing of a device.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eliminating recurrences' removes the two repeated Es from OVERSEE to leave OVERS, which 'repaired' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A servo is an automatic control device that amplifies a small force, as in power steering.

clue.text: News of missile landing on home

indicators.note: in a down clue, landing on means coming down on top of the following piece

parts.note: a bullet is a missile fired from a gun
in means at home

explanation.surface: News of a missile hitting a house.
explanation.definitionFit: A bulletin is a short official news report, as on radio or television.

clue.text: Noted slow progress of a soldier in 'trouble

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another, here the soldier inside the trouble

parts.note: ado means fuss or trouble
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: Someone noticed the sluggish advance of a soldier in difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noted' means written in musical notes: this is a slow movement or tempo in music.
explanation.definitionFit: Adagio is the musical marking for a slow tempo, so a passage played that way moves slowly.

clue.text: Genius dispatching wife to get chamois

indicators.note: dispatching means sending away, so one letter is removed from the genius word

parts.note: a genius is a wizard at something

explanation.surface: A clever person gets rid of his wife in exchange for a mountain goat.
explanation.definitionFit: The izard is the Pyrenean variety of the chamois, a goat-antelope of European mountains.

clue.text: Bottles out as result of such deliveries?

definitions.text: Bottles out as result of such deliveries?

parts.words: Bottles out as result of such deliveries?
parts.note: a milkman's daily route leaves bottles on doorsteps; 'bottles out' reads like losing nerve

explanation.surface: Someone loses their nerve because of certain deliveries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottles out' suggests the British slang for losing one's nerve, but here it is literal: milk bottles left out on doorsteps by a milkman on his daily delivery route.
explanation.definitionFit: A milkman's regular route leaves bottles of milk outside each house he serves.

clue.text: They tackle corruption in deputy's court

parts.note: vice means deputy, as in vice-captain, and the 's adds S
a quad is a quadrangle, a court enclosed by buildings

explanation.surface: Those fighting corruption appear in an assistant's courtroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A police unit dealing with gambling, prostitution and similar crime fights moral corruption.

clue.text: Prison officers occupied with old standard

parts.note: a standard is a flag or banner

explanation.surface: Prison staff are busy with an old-fashioned flag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prison officers' looks like warders, but the definition is a prison that officers occupied: a German camp for captured officers in the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: The German word is short for Offizierslager, a camp where captured military officers were held.

clue.text: Half the Navy regarded as a soft element?

definitions.text: Half the Navy regarded as a soft element?

parts.words: Half the Navy regarded as a soft element?
parts.note: the first half of the word Navy is Na, the chemical symbol of a soft metallic element

explanation.surface: Part of the fleet is thought a weak link.
explanation.walkthrough: The first two letters of 'Navy', Na, are the chemical symbol for this soft, silvery metal, which can be cut with a knife.
explanation.definitionFit: This alkali metal, symbol Na, is soft enough to cut with a knife.

clue.text: Sins you'd drunkenly perpetrated? Blame him!

indicators.note: drunkenly suggests the letters lurch about and land in a different order

parts.note: the apostrophe is dropped, leaving the letters Y, O, U and D

explanation.surface: If you sinned while drunk, put the blame on this figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunkenly perpetrated' rearranges SINS and YOUD.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek god of wine and revelry is the one to blame for drunken misdeeds.

clue.text: Dressed in braces?

parts.note: a brace is a pair, so being in braces means going in pairs, as animals into the Ark

explanation.surface: Someone is wearing trouser braces.
explanation.walkthrough: Braces suggest trouser straps (suspenders), but a brace is also a pair, so animals 'in braces' go in pairs, as into Noah's Ark.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes moving in pairs, one couple after another, like the animals boarding Noah's Ark.

clue.text: Having stickers distributed around the Hull area?

definitions.text: Having stickers distributed around the Hull area?

parts.words: Having stickers distributed around the Hull area?
parts.note: small sea creatures cling to a ship's underside; Hull also suggests the city in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Stickers are being handed out around the Yorkshire city of Hull.
explanation.walkthrough: Hull is a city in Yorkshire, but the hull here is a ship's: crustaceans that cling to it are the 'stickers'.
explanation.definitionFit: Barnacles are small crustaceans that stick to ships' bottoms, so a hull covered with them is described this way.

clue.text: Jack's wrong to get in the crop? It's hard to say

indicators.note: to get in says one piece goes inside another, here inside the crop

parts.note: a craw is a bird's crop, the pouch in its throat

indicators.note: wrong means the letters are out of their right order

parts.note: the 's is read as 'is', a link, leaving the name

explanation.surface: Jack is mistaken to step into the field of crops; that is hard to explain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' is the anagram signal and 'to get in' the container; the crop is a bird's throat pouch, not a field of grain, and a crackjaw word is a tongue-twister.
explanation.definitionFit: A crackjaw word is one difficult to pronounce, as if it might break the jaw.

clue.text: Parodies flawed proof? Yes

indicators.note: flawed suggests something faulty, so the letters are taken apart and set in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether spoofs are a sign of a defective proof, and answers yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flawed' rearranges PROOF and YES.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoofing means making humorous imitations, so the noun covers parodies and send-ups collectively.

clue.text: Read this to find out about your rate increase, in short

definitions.text: Read this to find out about your rate increase, in short

parts.words: Read this to find out about your rate increase, in short
parts.note: a dashboard instrument shows how fast you are going; 'in short' says the name is shortened

explanation.surface: A notice explains a rise in what you are charged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rate increase' looks like a bill, but the rate is your speed, shown on a dial whose long name is shortened.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortened name for the speedometer, the dial that shows a vehicle's velocity.

clue.text: Anger less than appropriate for such a person?

definitions.text: Anger less than appropriate for such a person?

parts.note: ire is a literary word for anger

indicators.note: less than means falling short of the whole word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: to appropriate is to nick, British slang for steal

explanation.surface: Showing less anger than a situation deserves is typical of this sort of person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less than' cuts the K from NICK to leave NIC. The whole clue also describes a peaceable person, who shows less anger than would be fitting.
explanation.definitionFit: A peace-seeking, conciliatory person shows less anger than a situation might warrant.

clue.text: Better spirits mixed here in drinking-vessel

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the drinking vessel

parts.note: a cup is a vessel for drinking from

indicators.note: mixed means the letters are blended into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Superior liquor is blended here in a cup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' is a verb here, to improve someone's spirits, not an adjective; 'mixed' is the anagram signal and 'in' the container.
explanation.definitionFit: To improve someone's mood or spirits is to make them more cheerful.

clue.text: I put in new altar for special form of worship

indicators.note: put in says the single letter is placed inside the rearranged word
new means the letters are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone installs a new altar for a particular style of worship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges ALTAR to LATRA, and 'put in' places I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: In Catholic theology latria is the supreme worship due to God alone.

clue.text: Extreme discomfort in alien country

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the other, here the pain inside the alien

parts.note: ET is the film alien, the extra-terrestrial
gyp is British slang for severe pain, as in 'my knee is giving me gyp'

explanation.surface: Severe discomfort is felt in a foreign land.
explanation.walkthrough: GYP is British informal for pain or trouble, as in 'my back is giving me gyp'.
explanation.definitionFit: Egypt is a nation of north-east Africa, home to the pyramids.

clue.text: In the end, married someone from south of India

indicators.note: In says one piece goes inside another, here the married abbreviation inside the end

parts.note: the tail is the end of something

explanation.surface: Eventually a person from southern India got married.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the end' reads as 'finally', but 'In' places M inside TAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tamils are a people of southern India and Sri Lanka.

clue.text: The fruit of rewriting parable with PC elements?

indicators.note: rewriting a text produces a new version, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: the elements of PC are its two letters, P and C

explanation.surface: A Bible story is reworked to make it politically correct, and this is the result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rewriting' rearranges PARABLE plus P and C.
explanation.definitionFit: A small sour fruit of a wild apple tree, used for jelly.

clue.text: First page on Roman law set up — minimal part screened

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the first piece sits above the next

parts.note: the first page of a book's preliminaries is numbered i, so page one is P I

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the letters are raised and read backwards

parts.note: lex is Latin for law

explanation.surface: A Roman law is printed on the first page, with only a tiny part on screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First page' is P (page) plus I (one in Roman numerals). 'set up' turns LEX to XEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A pixel is the smallest element of an image on a display screen.

clue.text: House elder brother for a bandleader

parts.note: drum is slang for a house or flat
in British public schools the elder of two brothers is called major, as in Smith major

explanation.surface: A man has a house and an older sibling to offer for a musical ensemble.
explanation.walkthrough: In British boarding schools brothers are told apart as major (elder) and minor (younger).
explanation.definitionFit: The person who leads a marching band, often twirling a mace or baton.

clue.text: Some influx originally appears here in 22

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of a flood of incomers first turns up in this place.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft had 'appears here in' as the definition, but 'appears' is a link and the definition is 'here in 22', a place in Egypt (the answer to 22 across).
explanation.definitionFit: Luxor is a city on the Nile in Upper Egypt, site of ancient Thebes.

clue.text: Alternative to booze, we hear, when deliveries are consistently blocked?

definitions.text: Alternative to booze, we hear, when deliveries are consistently blocked?

parts.words: Alternative to booze, we hear, when deliveries are consistently blocked?
parts.note: booze sounds like boos, another way a crowd shows displeasure; in cricket a batsman blocking every ball bores the spectators

explanation.surface: A drink-free option is suggested for when supplies keep being stopped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'booze' is said like 'boos', and a crowd can show displeasure by clapping slowly instead. In cricket, a batsman who just blocks each ball (delivery) is often greeted this way by bored spectators.
explanation.definitionFit: Slow rhythmic clapping is a crowd's way of showing impatience or disapproval, much as booing is.
